scope: Curated primary papers, documented datasets and explicitly labelled preprints checked for this release on 27 October 2026; not an exhaustive or automatically updated literature review.

articles.name: The organization of visual pathways in the Drosophila brain
articles.desc: Hoeller and colleagues use MaleCNS connectivity to trace visual pathways from optic lobes into the central brain. Network-derived receptive-field predictions are compared with physiological evidence; structural routes do not supply recorded activity for every cell.

articles.name: Sexual dimorphism in the complete Drosophila male central nervous system connectome
articles.desc: Cell study of the adult male brain and nerve cord: 166,700 annotated neurons, including 217 disconnected cells. Approximately 124.2 million predicted synaptic connections link the connected graph. Neuron proofreading does not mean each synapse was individually proofread.

articles.name: Distributed control circuits across a brain-and-cord connectome
articles.desc: Nature study of adult female brain-and-nerve-cord circuitry. Its published figure reports 155,916 proofread or roughly proofread neurons. Local sensory-effector loops are linked by long-range pathways. The specimen lacks lamina and ocellar tissue.

articles.name: Multiple Longitudinal Tracts in the Cephalopod Arm Sensorimotor System
articles.desc: Olson and Ragsdale describe longitudinal tracts using tracing and immunohistochemistry. Their anatomical findings suggest pathways for coordinating movements along an arm; they are not a whole-octopus synapse map or a validated control simulation.

articles.name: Dragonfly target-detecting neurons adapt to stimulus saliency
articles.desc: Vision Research experiments measure small-target neuron adaptation under changing contrast, direction and target jitter. These extracellular recordings motivate visual-processing concepts. The paper supplies no whole-dragonfly connectome; its experimental data are available on request.

articles.name: Neuronal segmentation in cephalopod arms
articles.desc: Olson, Schulz and Ragsdale identify repeated segments in octopus axial nerve cords and topographic organization associated with suckers. Image stacks and nerve-tracing data are linked by the paper. Anatomical modules do not establish individual synaptic connections.

articles.name: Neuronal wiring diagram of an adult brain
articles.desc: Dorkenwald and the FlyWire Consortium report 139,255 reconstructed neurons and approximately 54.5 million synaptic contacts in one adult female brain. This resource includes both optic lobes; it does not include the whole ventral nerve cord.

articles.name: Whole-brain annotation and multi-connectome cell typing of Drosophila
articles.desc: Schlegel and colleagues provide the companion FlyWire cell-type annotation framework and multi-connectome comparisons. A shared cell-type name is distinct from a shared neuron identifier; morphology and connectivity comparisons require specimen-aware matching.

articles.name: The connectome of an insect brain
articles.desc: Winding and colleagues reconstruct the larval Drosophila brain: 3,016 neurons and approximately 548,000 synapses. The study identifies recurrent motifs and multisensory pathways. Downloaded analytical matrices may cover filtered subsets and separate axonal or dendritic compartments.

articles.name: Virtual Fly Brain—An interactive atlas of the Drosophila nervous system
articles.desc: Court and colleagues describe an atlas integrating registered neuron images, anatomy, connectivity and expression evidence. The bundled larval skeletons use VFB’s shared L1EM reference frame and original CATMAID identifiers; per-neuron sources and licenses remain explicit.

articles.name: Recurrent architecture for adaptive regulation of learning in the insect brain
articles.desc: Eschbach and colleagues reconstruct recurrent pathways around the larval mushroom body. Public neuron reconstructions and adjacency matrices support structural circuit analysis. Synaptic routes motivate testable learning hypotheses; topology alone does not validate activity dynamics or behavioural effects of neuron removal.

articles.name: The complete connectome of a learning and memory centre in an insect brain
articles.desc: Eichler and colleagues map the larval mushroom body’s synaptic wiring, identifying stereotyped and variable organization in an associative circuit. Several bundled VFB cells belong to this reconstruction lineage; the eight-cell view remains a selected subset with separate export dates.

articles.name: Connectome quality converges predictably to reveal optimal stopping points during proofreading
articles.desc: Martinez and colleagues propose tracking graph invariants across actual proofreading snapshots. Their zebrafish and hemibrain analyses motivate explicit version histories. Convergence is a global proxy, not a measured error rate, biological change or validated stopping rule for every circuit.
articles.evidence: bioRxiv preprint v1, posted4 July2026; not peer reviewed

articles.name: Beyond Agreement: Standardizing Crowdsourced Synapse Annotations through Proofreading in EM Connectomics
articles.desc: Lee and colleagues combine explicit annotation criteria, rater calibration and probabilistic consensus in two larval EM volumes. The revised preprint reports remaining ambiguity and dataset-dependent agreement. Its eight-nanometre isotropic datasets are different from the bundled anisotropic L1EM patch.
articles.evidence: bioRxiv preprint v2, posted30 July2026; not peer reviewed

articles.name: SynAnno: Interactive Guided Proofreading of Synaptic Annotations
articles.desc: Lauenburg and colleagues present structured neuron-centred review, optimized traversal and a three-dimensional progress map. Seven experts evaluated the workflow. This research motivates inspectable annotation records; Synapse Atlas does not bundle SynAnno’s learned error-detection models or reproduce its validation study.

articles.name: CAVE: Connectome Annotation Versioning Engine
articles.desc: CAVE preserves queryable annotation and segmentation states while proofreading changes cell identities. Its time-aware services support reproducible analysis of large connectomes. Version identifiers and source receipts remain necessary even when a local workbench bundles only static snapshots.

articles.name: Connectomes across development reveal principles of brain maturation
articles.desc: Witvliet and colleagues reconstructed chemical connectivity across eight separate C. elegans specimens spanning larval stages and adulthood. Comparisons use identified cells and reveal both shared organization and variable wiring; cross-sectional specimens do not establish a longitudinal trajectory or causal developmental change.
